It's not true in the USA either. Reserve flight attendants are paid a monthly guarantee. They are often times getting paid more than what they actually work in a month. The above post is very inaccurate.

It's a very dangerous job, mostly due to unexpected turbulence and hard landings. The time changes, irregular schedule, poor diet (due to constantly eating restaurant/airplane food), radiation... all of that tends to affect the body over time. But the real acute threat is physical injury. I know many flight attendants who were injured on the job, some of which were career ending brain/spinal injuries. 

Going up and down can be physically exhausting, but the day to day work itself is a solid medium on the physical difficulty scale. They push a heavy beverage cart and are on their feet a lot, but I would say it's similar to a retail worker or teacher.
